title: Why sepsis bundle delivery differs between hospitals: a multi-site qualitative study of higher- and lower-performing sites
abstract: Objective: to identify determinants of timely antibiotic delivery for sepsis that distinguish higher- from lower-performing hospitals, by day and at night. Design: multi-site qualitative study at five hospitals with staff interviews and structured observation, coded with CFIR. Results and conclusions will be written after analysis.
introduction: Variation in time to antibiotics for sepsis between hospitals is common and worse at night, yet few studies explain it by comparing sites directly.
methods: Sites were contrasted using network figures. About 8 to 10 staff per site were interviewed and one day and one night shift observed. Summaries were coded with CFIR, constructs were rated by site, and higher- and lower-performing sites were compared.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present constructs by site, the high-low contrast and night-care findings.
discussion: The discussion will relate the determinants to strategies such as nurse-initiated protocols and antibiotic stock at triage, and state what the network should test next.
limitations: Staff accounts; five sites in one network; no patient interviews.
conclusion: To be written after analysis; it will name determinants, not claim effects of any strategy.
summary: SRQR-structured draft with results empty until fieldwork ends.
